correctness.rationale: For 0<lambda<1, a=1-lambda^2, and gamma>0, the entire symbol g_gamma(z)=int_0^1 t^(gamma-1)exp(i t z)dt is locally uniform by its convergent power series. Fock basis sum and Tonelli reduce the squared Hilbert–Schmidt norm to (1/pi)∫|g_gamma(x+iy)|²exp(-2ay²)dxdy. Fourier Plancherel for t^(gamma-1)1_(0,1)exp(-yt) is valid in L2 exactly gamma>1/2, including the distributional converse for gamma<=1/2; Gaussian y-integration yields sqrt(2pi/a)∫_0^1 t^(2gamma-2)exp(t²/(2a))dt. Each positive Fourier cutoff epsilon has finite HS norm; norm-change-of-variables inequality gives ||W_gamma-W_gamma,epsilon||<=epsilon^gamma exp(epsilon²/(4a))/(lambda gamma), proving ALL gamma>0 compact as norm limits. The Abelian elementary limit at gamma↓1/2 gives residue sqrt(2pi/a); cutoff integral gives logarithmic/power divergence. Independently evaluated gamma1, lambda=.6 finite HS integral ~4.182237539 as numerical normalization check; the infinite-dimensional result relies on the analytical proof, not that finite number.

value.rationale: An explicit compact yet non-Hilbert–Schmidt weighted composition operator directly addresses a posed compactness versus quadratic summability question in the classical Gaussian Fock model. Its sharp Fourier endpoint gamma=1/2, exact Hilbert–Schmidt integral, divergent cutoff energy, and quantitative compact approximations identify the mathematically meaningful ideal-theoretic boundary; this is not just a substitute for a known general criterion.
residual_risks: The claim does not classify all Schatten exponents or weighted Fock variants; that narrower scope does not erase the explicit counterexample value.

limitations: Classical Gaussian 1D Fock space; real 0<lambda<1, gamma>0, only Schatten 2; motivating and earlier criterion full texts partially inaccessible.
